question: How far can simulation stand in for testing this cast motor mount under a 2 kN belt pull?
context_of_use: A linear elastic static model of cast_motor_mount.step in Custom material (cast), under 2000 N -0.8660254,0,-0.5 at 0,-30,66 @ holes d=6.6, held by fixed z=min, used to judge the von Mises stress against 165 MPa with a target safety factor of 2.

factors.evidence: 13 of 13 strength cases with known answers pass their tolerance, run through the same pipeline, the largest error 4.3% (PLA shelf bracket, 6 mm fillet)

The mesh convergence check passes, von Mises stress settled: 122 -> 124 -> 124 MPa over 3 meshes, last change 0.1%. The force balance check passes, reactions balance the loads to 1e-05% (forces) and 1.2e-06% (moments)
every load, support and material was stated explicitly

The load introduction check reports the off part loads enter through a distributing coupling (the attached part adds no stiffness). The readings favour a distributed attachment over the other idealization by a likelihood ratio of more than 1,000, but the readings are synthetic, so this shows how a real test would settle it
factors.gap: measure where the idealizations differ most, so a test decides between them

factors.evidence: 4 inputs propagated with 200,000 samples by exact scaling of the converged solution: stress follows the load and not the modulus, deflection follows the load over the modulus. Of these, load drives most of the spread, total Sobol index 0.61
16 readings from readings.csv, synthetic and not from a real test, 16 with a stated uncertainty
factors.gap: test real parts with calibrated gauges (see the test plan)

factors.evidence: 16 of 16 readings within twice the validation uncertainty (ASME V&V 20), pooled area metric 0.121 against 0.145, but the readings are synthetic
factors.gap: compare with real readings, and agreement within the validation uncertainty sets this high

factors.evidence: 4 readings within 5 mm of the governing point, test loads reach 100% of the design load, the readings are synthetic
factors.gap: put a gauge at the governing point and test up to the design load

factors.evidence: probability of failure about 1 in 77 (1.3%, 95% interval 1.25% to 1.35%), and up to 0.013 across the idealizations Wobbl solved
factors.gap: the failure probability or the margin leaves too little room, so narrow the dominant input

disclaimer: Wobbl supplies credibility evidence and proposes levels. It does not certify the model, and the reviewer decides whether the evidence is enough for the decision.
headline: Model risk 4 of 5 (high influence, medium consequence), so Wobbl proposes a high goal for each factor. The evidence meets it on 4 of 9 factors. Short on model form, comparator, output comparison, applicability, uncertainty in the answer.
